preflight.note: Created before Tauri 2 desktop implementation began; activated only after WI053/WI054 completed with durable evidence and a Sol architecture review defined the desktop session, DTO, plan-handle, watcher, and capability boundaries.

acceptance_criteria.text: Create a Tauri 2 desktop application using a local Vite + React + TypeScript frontend as a consumer of reusable Rust core APIs; repository, validation, analysis, graph, and mutation semantics are not independently reimplemented in the web frontend.

Add a testable Rust desktop-adapter/service boundary, separate from Tauri macros and frontend code where practical, that owns frontend-safe DTO mapping, desktop repository/session state, plan-handle storage, service errors, and watcher integration while delegating governance semantics to the proven core crates.

Provide repository selection/open/switch through a Rust-side native directory picker and a native-owned active repository session; switching repositories stops the prior watcher, creates a new session generation, invalidates prior mutation-plan handles, and does not grant the frontend generic recursive filesystem authority.

Define stable serializable desktop repository/work/decision/evidence/validation/analysis/graph/mutation/event DTOs and mechanically generate or mechanically check the corresponding TypeScript contract from Rust so the frontend does not hand-maintain duplicate RepoPact domain enums or wire semantics.

Provide dashboard/health and navigation for Work, Decisions, Evidence, Graph, Validation, Analysis, and Settings using structured Rust-backed view models rather than frontend parsing/crawling of canonical repository files.

Implement work browsing/detail UX with lifecycle/scope/dependency filtering, search, acceptance-criterion/evidence state, source-backed relationships/analysis/frozen context, validation context, and advanced canonical raw representation that is read-only and resolvable only through core-indexed record identity rather than arbitrary filesystem paths.

Implement guided work-item creation covering title/intent, deterministic analysis, scope/ownership, dependencies, acceptance criteria, evidence expectations, governance/frozen review, core-generated mutation preview, and explicit apply without inventing a new `evidence_plan` schema field or other UI-only durable contract.

Implement WI054-supported typed work-item edit and lifecycle-transition workflows through plan/preview/apply; backend supplies canonical date/preflight inputs, no raw JSON write mode is introduced, and the UI does not invent a stricter lifecycle transition matrix than RepoPact's existing any-state-to-any-state post-validation model.

Keep executable `MutationPlan` objects in Rust memory and expose only a frontend `MutationPlanView` plus opaque handle/token; `apply_mutation_plan` retrieves the original plan by current desktop session, rechecks WI054 content-addressed preconditions, rejects stale/session-mismatched handles, and never executes caller-supplied path operations or a frontend-round-tripped raw plan.

Bound and lifecycle-manage the native plan registry: clear it on repository switch, invalidate successful/terminal plan handles as appropriate, require explicit re-plan after stale-plan failure, and introduce no persistent repository-local transaction/plan database or hidden journal.

Provide decision and evidence browse/detail UX from canonical Rust-backed records and graph relationships while preserving decision semantics and evidence durability/immutability; generic decision/evidence mutation is not introduced in WI055.

Expose relationship graph and deterministic analysis views derived from the core, with navigation to source records/basis and a keyboard/screen-reader-usable relationship list/table alternative; frontend layout libraries, if used, have presentation authority only.

Implement repository watching in Rust below the webview with path normalization, relevance classification, debounce/coalescing, safe session/snapshot refresh, typed repository-change events, repository-switch/shutdown cleanup, and bounded full-snapshot rebuild as a correctness fallback when incremental refresh is not safely available.

Self-originated mutation changes converge immediately to the authoritative post-apply view and later watcher events that resolve to the same snapshot/view token do not cause feedback loops or duplicate semantic refresh; external edits remain observable and invalid external states are surfaced rather than silently repaired.

Constrain the Tauri 2 command/capability surface using explicit application command permissions/manifest configuration and a local main-window capability; keep `withGlobalTauri` disabled, use local frontend assets/CSP, and expose no generic frontend filesystem, shell/process, arbitrary path traversal, or remote-origin authority.

Use a dedicated Rust-side native dialog operation for repository selection and grant frontend event listening only as needed for native repository-change notifications; generic dialog/filesystem JavaScript APIs and frontend event emission are not used as governance authority mechanisms unless separately justified and narrowed.

The desktop explicitly distinguishes its local Tauri application containment boundary from WI050 protected admission/operator/guard/enforcement/IPC/platform/protected-service authority and does not port, weaken, or claim equivalence to those security semantics.

Provide modern, responsive, information-dense and accessible UI behavior with keyboard navigation, visible focus, semantic labels/errors, non-color-only status, dark/light themes, reduced-motion consideration, accessible graph alternatives, and clear loading/empty/error/stale-plan/repository-refresh states.

Add executable desktop-adapter/frontend/security tests covering DTO binding drift, session replacement/stale-session rejection, plan-handle integrity/invalidation, watcher coalescing/refresh convergence, indexed raw-record path restriction, TypeScript checking, production frontend build, major UI workflows/accessibility, and Tauri capability assertions.

Run an end-to-end desktop smoke on the available host against a scratch adopted RepoPact repository proving open/browse/validate/analyze/graph, create/edit/transition plan+preview+apply, external-change refresh, stale-plan rejection, repository-switch stale-session/plan rejection, and final supported-state validation without using the development repository as an uncontrolled mutation fixture.

Preserve the WI054 baseline: Python install/tests, Rust workspace checks/tests, legacy alternate-implementation conformance, WI050 corpus, linked-worktree/reference behavior, frozen surface, and no unexpected Python semantic changes remain green after desktop implementation.

Record exact Windows/Linux/macOS execution and packaging status honestly: produce the available local desktop build/bundle on the development host when supported, distinguish unsigned local artifacts from production signing/notarization, avoid frozen CI/release changes without separate approval, and do not claim unexecuted platforms as validated.

Closeout evidence identifies the exact Tauri/Rust/frontend versions, application/crate layout, command and capability allowlists, DTO-generation mechanism, watcher/session/plan-handle architecture, UI workflows, test/build/E2E results, cross-platform/package status, known deferred surfaces, and confirmation that Python canonical-core cutover/WI050 migration remain separate work.
